newsitem.title: UK: Cap Gemini unveils new phone bill system.
newsitem.headline: Cap Gemini unveils new phone bill system.

text.p: French software engineer Cap Gemini Sogeti launched "Omilo", a software package designed to allow telephone companies to settle bills for calls made across different national borders, systems and technologies, the company said on Wednesday.

At a press conference, Cap Gemini, which says it is Europe's largest computer services company, said the rapid spread of deregulation and consumer choice has boosted telephone traffic, and widened it from voice to include data and multimedia business.

"Until now there has been no fully satisfactory means of calculating the resulting payments between telecoms companies, and this factor is inhibiting further expansion," Cap Gemini said in a statement.

The Omilo system automatically extracts and formats billing data, and allows telephone companies to assess profitability of their networks. Currently this data collection across different networks is handled manually an d involves high staff costs and delays, Cap Gemini said.

"With Omilo - which means "I speak" in ancient Greek - in place, real competition in global telecoms is cleared for takeoff," Brian Marshall, director of Cap Gemini Telecoms told the press conference.

Cap Gemini declined to say how much it had invested in the project, only saying that it had taken several man-years of work to develop. Clients would be charged an undisclosed fee based on the volume of traffic they generated.
"We have already sold the system already to one European operator," Marshall said.
